subject: barney
label: barney, in the place of the game's models/barney.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/hassassin.mdl, models/scientist.mdl, models/gman.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, D, B, C where the asset was A, C, C, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Outline matches the brief in all ten views: a standing man in a helmet, a black vest with SECURITY on front and back, and one arm held forward. No part sticks out or is missing in the side, back or angle views.

M2.reason: Measured 28.4 x 23.9 x 76 against the brief's 75 tall, 1.3% off, inside the 15% band. Nothing in the views contradicts the height.

M3.reason: Named parts: helmet, visor, vest, holster, shoes and hands. The helmet, vest, belt and holster (dark pouch on the right hip in front-right and right views) are there. The visor is not clear: the front view shows a dark band above the face that may be the visor, but it does not read as one at game size. Hands are mitts, as Valve's humans are.

M4.reason: Shirt is a blue, helmet blue, vest black and trousers blue-violet, as the brief says. But the back of each trouser leg has a light grey-white streak in the left, right, back and back-left views, and one hand (viewer's left, front view) reads white-grey rather than skin. Those regions are not the colour or material the brief asks for.

M5.reason: SECURITY lettering on the vest front and back reads clearly, and the helmet's star marking shows. Against that, the white streaks on the trousers and the grey-white shoe soles look like a smear or wear pattern the brief does not ask for, and they are clear in the walking frames.

M6.reason: Measured by the line-up test: the asset was picked 0 times in four readings (picks were C, D, B, C with the asset at A, C, C, B), so it passes. Capped at 2 as the rubric sets.

M7.reason: Front is the front: face, chest pockets and the holster side are where a front view puts them, and SECURITY is on the back. It stands upright on its origin, with feet on the floor in the side and front views.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. 650 triangles is under the 731 that three quarters of Half-Life's kind have and under twice the median of 504. The hands and body join at the sides, and nothing floats in the views a player sees. The pale wedge is painted and not a loose or inside-out face, so it is charged to M4 and M5.

C1.reason: In the 22-frame run and the 8-frame attack, the arms, legs, head and vest stay on the body, and the arm and hand move with the torso. Nothing comes apart, sinks or floats. The attack is small in movement, but nothing detaches.
